guidance: Only the letters and digits count. Capital and small letters count as the same, and punctuation doesn't count: if the readings differ only in a comma or a capital, compare the letters.
On older pages the long s (ſ), which looks like an f without the bar across, counts as s: a reading with f in its place does not match.
If the box cuts off part of the word, look at the line above it to see the whole word.
If a letter is too worn or blotted to tell which reading it supports, pick Can't tell.

A printed fraction such as ½: if neither reading has it, pick Neither, then type the word in the box. The ⌨ button beside Send shows buttons for ½ ¼ ¾ and other characters a keyboard lacks, and 1/2 typed out counts the same.
intro: These come from English-language newspaper pages in Chronicling America, the Library of Congress's collection of historic American newspapers. Most are words where two machine readings (OCR) disagree. Some ask instead whether a drawn line runs between two columns, or whether a machine reading missed any of a block of print: those cards say what to look for.
